informationArchitecture:
FILE AND BUILD POSTURE

Ship it exactly the way `public/product/investor/deck.site.html` ships: one standalone, fully pre-rendered static HTML file at `public/product/compliance/checklist.site.html`, fonts preloaded from `../fonts/`, one inline `<style>` block, one committed dark identity with every colour painted explicitly. Two differences from the deck:

1. The page is GENERATED at build time from `public/product/compliance/compliance.json` (same relationship deck.site.html has to deck-plan.json). Every item, jurisdiction and fact is in the JSON; the HTML is the render. This keeps the data diffable in git, keeps the page renderable with JS off, and lets the lawyer print a complete document.
2. It carries a small amount of vanilla JS (filters, tick persistence, progress recompute, prerequisite enforcement, print prep). JS is progressive enhancement only — with JS disabled every panel is open, every item visible, nothing is lost. Never a framework, never a fetch.

Token declaration: the standalone page cannot import `app/theme/tokens.css`, so it re-declares the Floodlight DARK values under the CANONICAL token names in `:root` — `--bg-0:#0a0e14; --bg-1:#121821; --bg-2:#1a222e; --line:rgba(82,92,108,.6); --text:#f7f6ef; --muted:#a6adba; --volt:#d4ff3a; --ember:#ff7a2f; --cyan:#4ee1ff; --gold:#ffc83d; --magenta:#ff5ea8; --danger:#ff4d4d;` plus every `--*-soft` / `--*-ink` / `--*-text` twin, the radii (`--r-control:10px; --r-card:16px; --r-hero:24px; --r-pill:999px`), the three font stacks, the full `--fs-12 … --fs-64` scale and `--gutter:16px`, copied verbatim from `app/theme/tokens.css`. Name-for-name identity with the app is the point: a later port into the app is a copy, not a translation. One permitted local addition: `--dim: #6f7987` (tertiary mono text), matching deck.site.html's `--dim`. No raw hex anywhere below `:root`.

Deviation from the deck, deliberate and to be kept: the deck's 10.5px mono kickers are NOT carried over. Nothing on this page is smaller than `--fs-12` (12px). This is a working document read on a phone by a founder and printed by a lawyer; 10.5px fails both.

THREE READERS, THREE ENTRY POINTS

The page serves the founder (daily: what do I do next), the lawyer (top-to-bottom, printed, wants the question list and the evidence), and the investor (posture and honesty: is this person kidding themselves). All three entry points sit in the first screen or one tap from it.

PAGE ORDER

§00 Masthead — `<header>`. Title FACT//DUEL COMPLIANCE. One-line what-this-is. Then four mono facts on one row (wrapping to two at 390px): AS OF <date> · REGIONS 3 · ITEMS <n> · UNVERIFIED <n>. Then the global three-segment progress meter with its full mono label. Then the standing disclaimer block, always visible, never collapsed: "This is an operational working file, not legal advice. No money is taken by FACT//DUEL today. Ticks are this device's local record, not a legal record." Then a `.fd-actions` row: Clear ticks · Copy status as Markdown · Print.

§01 NEXT FIVE — the founder's view, and deliberately the first content on the page. Computed at build time (and recomputed by JS from live tick state): the five items that are not done, not blocked, in the shortest-lead-time order. Rendered as five full checklist rows, not a summary list, so they are actionable in place. Each carries a "why now" line: "longest lead time in the US path — everything in Stage 2 waits on it." If fewer than five qualify, the block shows what it has and says so; if zero, it shows the earliest blocking item instead with the text "Nothing is unblocked. The next thing to unblock is —".

§02 HOW TO READ THIS PAGE — the legend. Deliberately early, not an appendix, because a lawyer reads top-down and a chip is meaningless until it is defined. Contains: the legal-posture scale (5 chips), the work-status scale (5 chips), the UNVERIFIED rule stated in one sentence, the ref-code convention, and the sentence "Verification is a separate axis from status: an item can be CLEAR and UNVERIFIED at the same time, and this page will always show you both."

§03 THE DECISION MATRIX — four candidate product models × three regions, twelve cells. This is the lawyer's and the investor's entry point and the top of the "which market" funnel. Every cell is a link into the region section, anchored at that model's verdict. Below the matrix, one paragraph naming the four models in full with their fixed letters, which never change anywhere on the page:
 M1 Free play, no purchase — the current product; simulated coins, no cash in, no cash out.
 M2 Paid entry, prize pool — entry fee, cash prizes.
 M3 Subscription, operator-funded prizes — no per-entry stake.
 M4 Free entry, sponsored prizes — sweepstakes shape with an alternate method of entry.
Models are ordered by ascending risk and always appear in that order. Models never carry a colour; they carry letters. Colour belongs to status only.

§04 THE COMMON GATE — everything that must exist before any region-specific filing: operating entity, bank and payment-service provider, KYC/AML programme, age assurance, geolocation, responsible-play controls, terms and privacy, tax registration, records retention. Placed before the regions because it is the top of the prerequisite graph and every regional Stage 2 item depends on something here. Rendered as checklist rows grouped by stage.

§05 UNITED STATES · §06 EUROPEAN UNION · §07 INDIA — three identical region sections, same internal order every time so the reader learns it once:
 (a) Region header card: posture sentence, the model verdict strip (M1–M4 chips, each with a one-line reason and a link to the governing item), the region's own progress meter, and the region's cost total and longest lead time in mono.
 (b) The jurisdiction grid — 51 tiles for the US (50 states + DC; if territories are in scope the count and the list change and the heading says so), 27 for the EU, and for India the state grid is not optional either: Indian state law varies materially, so India gets a grid of its states and union territories with the same component and the same statuses.
 (c) The region's checklist, grouped by STAGE in execution order, and this grouping is the answer to "what do I file":
   Stage 0 — Entity and money rails
   Stage 1 — Legal opinion / regulator engagement
   Stage 2 — Licences, registrations, notifications
   Stage 3 — Product controls that must ship before launch
   Stage 4 — Ongoing obligations after launch
 (d) The region's open questions (a filtered view of §09).

§08 THE FILING REGISTER — every filing on the page in one flat table: ref, jurisdiction, item, issuer, cost, lead time, prerequisite, status, verified. Sortable by lead time and by cost. This is the single sheet the lawyer prints and marks up, and it is the only horizontally scrolling element on the page.

§09 OPEN QUESTIONS FOR COUNSEL — every UNVERIFIED fact on the page, collected automatically, each phrased as a question and each carrying its "what would settle it" line and a back-link to the row it came from. Numbered Q1…Qn so they can be answered by number in an email. This section exists because the honest thing to do with an unverified fact is not to hide it or hedge it but to turn it into a billable question.

§10 CRITICAL PATH — the items ordered by lead time with their dependency chain, so the founder can see that a 180-day licence started today lands in month seven. Text and mono numbers, not a Gantt chart; a chart here would be decoration.

§11 EVIDENCE — every source with the date it was last checked, in the deck's `.sources` style.

§12 CHANGE LOG — dated entries, newest first. A compliance file with no change log is not trustworthy.

NAVIGATION AND THE "WHICH MARKET → WHAT DO I FILE" PATH

A sticky sub-bar under the masthead carries, on one row at every width: a three-segment region switcher (USA / EU / INDIA — anchor links, not tabs, so the page stays one printable document) and, at ≥900px, a compact copy of the active region's progress meter. Selecting a region scrolls to its section and sets `data-region` on `<html>`, which dims nothing and hides nothing — it only drives the filter chips' defaults.

The documented path is three taps:
 1. Region switcher, or a matrix cell if the reader is choosing between models.
 2. Region header → the model verdict strip says which of M1–M4 is even available here, with the one-line reason.
 3. Stage list → the filings, in the order they must be done, each with issuer, cost, lead time and its prerequisite as a live link.

A fourth tap drills deeper: tapping a jurisdiction tile opens that jurisdiction's panel, which lists only the items THAT jurisdiction adds on top of the region baseline, each as a link to the full row in the stage list. Jurisdiction panels never duplicate the item detail — one item exists in exactly one place and everything else points at it by ref code.

REF CODES

Every item has a stable, human-quotable code: `US-FED-03`, `US-NV-MTL`, `EU-MT-B2C`, `IN-TN-02`, `GATE-04`. The code is the element `id` (lowercased, `f-` prefixed: `id="f-us-nv-mtl"`), it is printed in mono next to the item title, it is what every cross-reference and back-link uses, and it is what the lawyer cites in a reply. Codes are assigned in the JSON and never reused after deletion.

STATE PERSISTENCE

`localStorage` key `fd.compliance.v1` holding `{ checked: {ref: ISODate}, view: 'grid'|'list', filters: {...} }`, every read and write inside try/catch, and the page renders correctly when it throws or returns nothing. Ticks store the date they were set so the row can print "done 2026-10-04". The masthead says plainly that ticks are device-local.

components.name: Status chip (fd-chip)
components.purpose: The single atom of status on the page, used in the matrix, on jurisdiction tiles, on checklist rows and in the legend. Two closed families, never mixed on one element. FAMILY A — legal posture, applies to a place or a place×model: CLEAR (glyph ✓, volt), CONDITIONAL — permitted only with a licence, registration or structural change (glyph ◆, gold), PROHIBITED (glyph ✕, ember), CONTESTED — law ambiguous, litigation live, or a regulator has taken a contrary view (glyph !, magenta), UNKNOWN — not researched (glyph –, dim). FAMILY B — work status, applies to a checklist row: DONE (✓, volt), IN PROGRESS (◐, cyan), BLOCKED (⊘, ember), NOT STARTED (○, dim), NOT APPLICABLE (—, dim, label struck through). Rules: the label word is always visible text, never a title attribute or an aria-label alone; colour is never the only carrier, the glyph and the word are; a row carries at most one chip per family; PROHIBITED and BLOCKED share ember but never appear in the same context and have different glyphs and different words, which is the disambiguation.
components.markup: ◆CONDITIONAL Interactive variant (filter chips only) is a real
components.tokens: display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:6px; padding:4px 10px; border-radius:var(--r-pill); font-family:var(--font-mono); font-size:var(--fs-12); line-height:1.25; letter-spacing:.08em; text-transform:uppercase; white-space:nowrap; min-height:24px. Per status: background var(--gold-soft), colour var(--gold-text), border 1px solid color-mix(in oklab, var(--gold) 45%, transparent) — and the same pattern with volt / ember / magenta. UNKNOWN and NOT STARTED: background var(--bg-2), colour var(--dim), border 1px dashed var(--line). Glyph inherits colour and sits at font-size:1em with font-variant-numeric:normal. The --*-text twins are used for the ink, never the raw fill token, so the light-theme port and print both work unchanged.
components.mobile: Unchanged below 600px — the chip never shrinks below --fs-12 and never drops its label. Where horizontal room runs out the chip wraps to its own line above the item title rather than truncating. In the jurisdiction grid the chip is not used at all; the tile shows the glyph alone plus screen-reader text (see fd-tile). Filter chips (fd-chip--btn) get padding-block:10px so the hit area is ≥44px tall, and the row of them scrolls horizontally with scroll-snap-type:x proximity rather than wrapping to four lines.

components.name: UNVERIFIED treatment (fd-unverified / .fd-u)
components.purpose: Makes an unverified fact impossible to read past, and does it without spending a colour, because verification is a SECOND AXIS orthogonal to status — an item can be CLEAR and UNVERIFIED simultaneously. The whole verification layer is achromatic (ink + hatch + a border), so it never collides with the chromatic status layer, it survives colour-blindness by construction, and it prints in black on a mono laser printer with no loss. Two forms: the block form fd-unverified marks a whole row, cell or tile; the inline form .fd-u marks a single value inside otherwise-verified prose (a cost, a lead time, a date).
components.markup:
Block form — sits inside the row it qualifies, immediately after the status chip, never below the fold of the row:

UNVERIFIED That a federal MSB registration is required for M2. Settles it: FinCEN 31 CFR 1010.100(ff) read against the prize-pool flow, or written counsel. Question 7

The containing row gets data-verify="unverified", which paints the hatched left rule. Inline form — for one value:
$5,000 approx.
Every unverified fact in the JSON MUST carry a `settles` string. The build fails if one is missing. "Unverified" without "what would settle it" is a shrug, not a disclosure — this mirrors the convention already used in public/product/investor/numbers.md.
components.mobile: At ≤599px the block form stacks to three lines inside the 4px hatched rule: tag, what, settles. The settles line is never collapsed behind a disclosure on any width — that is the sentence that makes the disclosure useful. The Question link is a 44px-tall tap target on its own line. The inline .fd-u keeps its dotted underline and its trailing "?" ; its data-settle is exposed on tap by moving that text into the live region, because title tooltips do not exist on touch.

components.name: Decision matrix (fd-matrix)
components.purpose: Four product models × three regions, twelve cells. The lawyer's and the investor's entry point, and the funnel from 'which market' into a region section. Each cell states the posture and one reason and links onward. It is genuinely tabular data, so it is a real <table> at every width, with the display-change roles restored explicitly so semantics survive the mobile restyle.

components.name: Progress (fd-progress)
components.purpose: Honest completion. Three segments, never one number: done on a verified basis, done on an unverified basis, and remaining. An item that is ticked but whose legal basis is UNVERIFIED does NOT count toward the verified segment — that is the page's honesty guardrail expressed as arithmetic. There is also a blocked count in the label, because 9 blocked items is the most useful number on the page and a bar cannot show it.
components.markup:
14/38 done · 6 on an unverified basis · 9 blocked

The label text is never omitted and never abbreviated to a bare percentage. If a percentage is shown anywhere, the unverified count is shown in the same breath.

mobileRules:
GLOBAL

- Mobile-first CSS. Breakpoints match the Floodlight skill: 600 (phone landscape), 900 (the layout's major change), 1200 (wide). Everything is written for 390px first and widened.
- Gutters: `padding-inline: max(var(--gutter), env(safe-area-inset-left)) / …right`, applied once on one outer `.fd-shell` wrapper, never as a `padding` shorthand that could zero the sides. `main { max-width: 1100px; margin-inline: auto }`.
- Zero horizontal overflow at 390px is a release gate, verified the way the skill prescribes: dev server, `node scripts/screens.mjs`, then read the PNGs. No element anywhere sets a `min-width` wider than the viewport except `.fd-register` inside its `overflow-x:auto` wrap. Every grid track uses `minmax(0, 1fr)`; every `dd`, issuer name and URL carries `overflow-wrap: anywhere`.
- `body { padding-block-end: calc(72px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px)) }` so the last item clears the on-screen furniture and the home indicator.
- `scroll-padding-top: 104px` (the sticky bar's two-row height plus 8px) so anchor jumps from the matrix, the grid and the question list never land under the bar. This is the most commonly missed detail on a page built out of anchors — it must be set.
- Heading sizes need no mobile overrides: `--fs-28` and `--fs-36` are clamps that already resolve to 1.5rem and 1.8rem at 390px. Do not add media-query font sizes on top of the clamps.
- `text-wrap: balance` on h1–h4, `text-wrap: pretty` on ledes and note paragraphs.
- Touch: `touch-action: manipulation` and `-webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent` on tiles, chips, labels and summaries. Press feedback is a background change to `var(--bg-2)` on `:active` — no transform, no scale, no transition. This page is a document being worked through, not a game screen; the answer-button press vocabulary does not apply here.
- Every interactive element is ≥44×44 CSS px, achieved with padding or an absolutely positioned label overlay, never by growing the visible glyph.

THE 51-ROW GRID AT 390px — the hard case

Arithmetic: 390 − 32 (gutters) = 358 available; `gap: 6px`; `grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(64px, 1fr))` ⇒ 5 columns at ~66px each. 51 tiles ⇒ 11 rows at 52px + 10 gaps ≈ 632px. That is one and a bit phone screens, and it is the right trade: the heat-map is the fastest way to see "three states are red" and it survives at that density because each tile carries only a two-letter code and one glyph.

Rules that make it survive:
1. Never fewer than 4 columns. If the container ever computes to 3 or fewer (a 320px device, or a browser at 200% zoom), the grid switches to list view automatically via `@media (max-width: 359px)` — below that width the heat-map stops reading and the list is genuinely better.
2. A `.fd-skip` link is the first focusable element inside the grid group: "Skip the 51-state grid" → jumps to the region's stage list. Same for the 27 and for India.
3. A "List view" toggle sits in the grid's header bar at every width, remembered in localStorage. List view is one column of 44px rows: full jurisdiction name, status chip, item count, sorted PROHIBITED → CONTESTED → CONDITIONAL → CLEAR → UNKNOWN. Grid is the default because scanning is the grid's job; the list is one tap away for working.
4. Opening a tile's panel inserts a `grid-column: 1 / -1` sibling directly after that tile. At ≤719px only one panel is open at a time — opening a second closes the first — so the grid never becomes a 51-section accordion the reader has to scroll back through. At ≥720px any number may be open.
5. The 27-item EU grid is 6 rows at 390px and needs nothing special. India's grid uses the identical component and sizes itself the same way.
6. The grid never scrolls horizontally, never sets a min-width, and never truncates a code.

THE WIDE MATRIX AT 390px

The 4×3 matrix does NOT scroll sideways and does NOT shrink. It reflows, with no duplicated markup, by switching the table's display at ≤719px:

- `table, thead, tbody, tr, th, td { display: block }`, with `role="table" / "rowgroup" / "row" / "columnheader" / "rowheader" / "cell"` already present in the HTML so the table semantics survive the display change for assistive technology. This is not optional — a `display:block` table silently loses its role.
- `thead` becomes `.fd-sr` (clipped, not `display:none`, so it stays in the accessibility tree).
- Each `<tr>` becomes a card: `var(--bg-1)`, 1px `var(--line)`, `var(--r-card)`, 14px padding, 12px bottom margin.
- The row header (`M2 Paid entry, prize pool`) is the card's title.
- Each `<td>` becomes a row inside the card at `grid-template-columns: 64px minmax(0,1fr)`, with the region name injected from `data-region-label` in mono `--fs-12` `--dim`.
- The phone read becomes "for M2: USA CONDITIONAL / EU CONDITIONAL / India CONTESTED" — a within-model comparison, which is the comparison a founder actually makes on a phone. At ≥720px it is a conventional grid where the cross-region scan is easy because the columns align.
- Optional refinement: when the sticky switcher has a region selected, JS may set `hidden` on the two non-selected `td` rows inside each card. Default with no selection is all three.

OTHER REFLOWS AT ≤599px

- `.fd-facts` (issuer / cost / lead time / prerequisite): 4 columns at ≥900, 2 at 600–899, and at ≤599 a single column where each pair is its own `92px minmax(0,1fr)` grid — label left, value right, values column-aligned down the card. Stacking `dt` over `dd` would turn one row into eight lines; it is banned.
- Region summary `dl`: three columns → one column of `110px minmax(0,1fr)` pairs.
- Legend `dl`: `160px 1fr` → single column with 1px rules between pairs.
- Filing register: `<details>` closed by default; the only horizontal scroll on the page, with `tabindex="0"`, an accessible name and a right-edge fade.
- Filter chips: one horizontally scrolling row with `scroll-snap-type: x proximity`, never four wrapped lines.
- Notes `<details>` inside items: closed at <1200px, open by default at ≥1200px.
- The sticky bar is two rows (~96px + safe-area) at ≤899px, one row at ≥900px.

MOTION

There is none, by decision. The only permitted transitions are 120ms `background-color`/`color` on hover and focus of interactive elements. `<details>` opens instantly. The progress meter updates instantly — the reader caused the change and 400ms of easing reads as lag. Nothing enters, nothing lifts, nothing shakes, nothing counts up. The `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { *, *::before, *::after { transition: none !important; animation: none !important; scroll-behavior: auto !important } }` guard is present anyway, matching deck.site.html, because a future edit will otherwise reintroduce motion.
accessibility:
TARGET: WCAG 2.2 AA, with 2.5.8 target size applied at the stricter 44×44 level throughout.

COLOUR AND MEANING
- No status is ever carried by colour alone. Every chip is colour + a distinct glyph + the word. Every jurisdiction tile is tint + glyph + screen-reader text. The five posture glyphs (✓ ◆ ✕ ! –) and five work glyphs (✓ ◐ ⊘ ○ —) are distinguishable in monochrome, which is also what makes print work.
- The verification axis is deliberately ACHROMATIC — hatch, ink and border only — so it can co-occur with any status colour without collision and survives every form of colour vision deficiency and every mono printer.
- Ink always uses the `--*-text` twins, never the raw fill tokens. In the standalone dark page the twins equal the accents, which already clear 4.5:1 on `--bg-0/1/2`; if the page is ever ported to the light theme, the twins are already the right values and nothing needs rewriting.
- Contrast floors: body and all labels ≥4.5:1, including the 12px mono chip and `dt` labels — 12px is not "large text" and takes no 3:1 exemption. Chip ink is checked against its own `-soft` tint, not against the page ground, because the tint is what sits behind it. Non-text UI (tile borders, the progress track, checkbox borders) ≥3:1 against its adjacent surface. `--dim: #6f7987` is used ONLY on `--bg-0` and `--bg-1` where it clears 4.5:1; it is never placed on `--bg-2` inside a tinted chip.
- `@media (prefers-contrast: more)`: all `-soft` tint backgrounds drop to `var(--bg-1)`, every border goes to 1px solid `color-mix(in oklab, var(--text) 70%, transparent)`, and the dotted `.fd-u` underline goes solid 2px.

STRUCTURE AND SEMANTICS
- `<html lang="en">`. One `<h1>`. Headings strictly h1 → h2 (region / major section) → h3 (grid, stage) → h4 (jurisdiction panel), no skipped levels ever.
- Landmarks: `<header>`, a `<nav aria-label="Regions">` inside the sticky bar, `<main>`, one `<section aria-labelledby>` per major section, `<footer>`. A skip-to-content link is the first element in the DOM.
- The matrix and the register are real `<table>` elements with `<caption>`, `<th scope="col">` and `<th scope="row">`. Where the matrix is restyled to blocks at ≤719px, explicit `role="table|rowgroup|row|columnheader|rowheader|cell"` attributes are present in the HTML so the semantics survive `display:block`.
- The jurisdiction grid is a `<div role="group" aria-label="United States — 51 jurisdictions">` containing 51 real `<button>` elements. Each tile's accessible name comes from visible text plus a `.fd-sr` span ("Washington — prohibited — 2 items, 0 unverified"), not from `aria-label`, so it survives translation and in-page find.
- Disclosure: tiles use `aria-expanded` + `aria-controls` pointing at a panel with `role="region" aria-labelledby="<tile id>"`. Item notes use native `<details>`/`<summary>` with no ARIA added.
- `<time datetime>` on every checked-on and target date.

KEYBOARD
- Everything reachable and operable by keyboard in DOM order. No keyboard traps, no roving-tabindex scheme in the grid: 51 sequential buttons is a legitimate list of controls, and the cost of it is paid by the skip link that is the first focusable element inside each grid group.
- Focus: `:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--volt); outline-offset: 3px; border-radius: inherit }` globally; grid tiles override to `outline-offset: 2px` so the ring is not clipped by the 6px gap. Outlines are never removed, and `:focus:not(:focus-visible)` is the only thing allowed to suppress them.
- Opening a jurisdiction panel moves nothing; focus stays on the tile (which now reads `aria-expanded="true"`), and the panel is the tile's next sibling so it is the next thing in reading and tab order.
- `aria-sort` on the register's sortable column headers, updated on activation.

THE PREREQUISITE RULE — the a11y-critical decision
A checklist item whose prerequisite is unmet uses `aria-disabled="true"`, NOT the `disabled` attribute. A `disabled` input cannot receive focus, which makes the reason it is disabled unreachable to a screen-reader user — the exact information they need. So the checkbox stays focusable, carries `aria-describedby` pointing at the visible "Blocked by GATE-01 US entity + EIN" line, and a click or Enter is intercepted, ignored, and announced in the live region.

LIVE REGIONS
One polite, atomic live region (`#fd-live`, `aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true"`, visually hidden) announces exactly four kinds of event and nothing else:
1. Filter results — "18 items shown, 20 hidden by 2 filters."
2. A tick — "Marked done. United States 15 of 38, 6 on an unverified basis."
3. A blocked tick attempt — "Blocked by GATE-01, US entity and EIN."
4. An unblock — "GATE-01 done. US-NV-MTL is now unblocked."
The progress meter itself is `role="img"` with a full `aria-label` sentence rather than a live region, so it does not double-announce.

CONTENT ACCESSIBILITY
- Jurisdiction codes are two-letter abbreviations; the full name is always in the tile's accessible name and always visible in list view and in the panel heading. `<abbr>` is used for ISO codes in prose.
- Link text is never "here" or "see". In-page links carry their ref code as text. External links open in a new tab and say so in a `.fd-sr` span ("opens in a new tab").
- No tooltip-only information anywhere: `title` is never the sole carrier of anything, because it does not exist on touch and is unreliable with AT. The `.fd-u` inline marker's `data-settle` text is surfaced into the live region on activation.
- Copy tone follows the Floodlight rule: plain, no shaming, no "unfortunately". A prohibited state is stated, not apologised for.

ZOOM AND REFLOW
- Content reflows to a single column with no loss of function and no two-dimensional scrolling at 320px width / 400% zoom, with the sole exception of the filing register (a data table, which 1.4.10 explicitly permits) — and the register's data is also available as the fd-item cards, so nothing is only in the table.
- No `user-scalable=no`, no `maximum-scale`. The viewport meta is exactly `width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover`, matching deck.site.html.
- The page is usable with JavaScript off: every panel open, every item visible, nothing hidden behind a script. Filtering and ticking are the only things lost.

MOTION AND SENSORY
- No animation exists on the page. The `prefers-reduced-motion` guard is present regardless as a defence against future edits. Nothing flashes; there is no content that could trigger 2.3.1.
- No audio, no autoplay, no timing, no session limit, nothing that expires.
print:
The lawyer's copy is a first-class output, not an afterthought. Printing this page must produce a complete, self-explanatory, markable document with nothing hidden and nothing lost.

PAGE SETUP
`@page { margin: 16mm 14mm }` and deliberately NO `size` declaration, so the same file prints correctly on A4 (the EU and Indian readers) and US Letter (the American lawyer). Nothing on the page is sized in a way that assumes one or the other.

PALETTE INVERSION
Inside `@media print`, redefine the tokens at `:root` — `--bg-0:#fff; --bg-1:#fff; --bg-2:#f4f4f4; --line:#999; --text:#000; --muted:#333; --dim:#555` — and map every accent's `-text` twin to near-black greys (`--volt-text:#000; --ember-text:#000; --gold-text:#000; --magenta-text:#000; --cyan-text:#000`) with the `-soft` tints going to `transparent`. Status is then carried entirely by the glyph and the word, which is why the glyph-plus-word rule exists. Do not rely on `print-color-adjust` for status; the one exception is the UNVERIFIED rule, which becomes a solid 2px black left border (no hatch — hatching is unreliable at print DPI) with `print-color-adjust: exact` on that rule only.

REVEAL EVERYTHING
On `beforeprint` (and mirrored in CSS for the no-JS case):
- `document.querySelectorAll('details').forEach(d => { d.dataset.wasOpen = d.open; d.open = true })`, restored on `afterprint`.
- Every jurisdiction panel has its `hidden` attribute removed; every tile's `aria-expanded` goes true.
- Every filter is cleared, so a filtered screen never prints as a partial document. A short line is printed at the top of the register section: "Printed unfiltered — 3 filters were active on screen."
- `.fd-item[hidden]` and any other `[hidden]` set by filtering is forced visible with `display:revert !important`.

CHECKBOX STATE MUST PRINT
Native checkbox `:checked` rendering is unreliable across print engines, so in print the real input is `display:none` and the state is drawn as text: `.fd-item[data-done="true"] .fd-item__mark::after { content: "[x]" }` / `[data-done="false"] { content: "[ ]" }` in `var(--font-mono)` at `--fs-14`. A done item also prints its date: `.fd-item[data-done="true"] .fd-item__title::after { content: " — done " attr(data-done-on) }`.

PRINT COVER BLOCK
A `.fd-printhead` that is `display:none` on screen and `display:block` in print, forced onto its own first page (`break-after: page`), carrying: the title, the as-of date, the print date (`content: ""` cannot generate it, so JS writes it on `beforeprint`), the item and unverified counts, and three lines of standing text — "Operational working file. Not legal advice." / "Tick marks are one device's local record, not a legal record." / "Every fact marked UNVERIFIED is collected as a numbered question in section 09." The lawyer must learn all of that before page two.

WHAT IS DROPPED
`display: none` in print for: the sticky bar, the region switcher, the filter chips, the view toggle, the skip links, the action buttons (Clear ticks / Copy / Print), the sort buttons (their column headers print as plain text), and the register's right-edge scroll fade.

LINKS PRINT THEIR TARGETS
- In-page: `a[href^="#"]::after { content: " [" attr(data-ref) "]" }` — every cross-reference prints the ref code it points at, so "Blocked by GATE-01" is followed by the code and can be found by eye.
- External: `a[href^="http"]::after { content: " (" attr(href) ")"; font-size: 8.5pt; word-break: break-all; color: #333 }`. Evidence with no printable URL is useless to a diligence reader.

PAGINATION
- `break-before: page` on each `section.fd-region`, on §08 the register, and on §09 the questions.
- `break-inside: avoid` on `.fd-item`, `.fd-juris`, `.fd-question`, `.fd-legend__set > div`, `.fd-region-head`, and every table row.
- `thead { display: table-header-group }` on the register so column headers repeat on every page; `tfoot` unused.
- `h2, h3 { break-after: avoid }` so no heading is orphaned at a page foot.
- `orphans: 3; widows: 3` on body text.

COMPONENT-SPECIFIC PRINT BEHAVIOUR
- The jurisdiction grid does NOT print as a 5-column heat-map; tints are gone in print and a grid of bare codes is unreadable. It becomes a two-column flowed list: `.fd-grid { display: block; columns: 2; column-gap: 10mm }` with each tile becoming a full-width line `grid-template-columns: 30px 1fr auto` reading `WA  Washington  PROHIBITED`, followed by its now-visible panel at `column-span: all`. All 51 print, in order, complete.
- The matrix prints in its ≥720px table form regardless of the screen width it was printed from — force `.fd-matrix { display: table }` and reinstate the `thead` — because a printed page is always wide enough and the 4×3 grid is the most useful thing on the first content page. Give it `break-inside: avoid` and 1px `#999` cell borders.
- The register prints in full at `font-size: 8.5pt`, `min-width: 0`, `overflow: visible` — no scroll box on paper, ever.
- The progress meter prints as its text label only; the 8px track is `display: none` (a grey bar at print DPI says nothing).
- Base print type: `font-size: 10.5pt; line-height: 1.45` on body, `--fs-*` left to resolve as-is for headings; the mono 12px labels land near 9pt, which is the floor.
unverifiedTreatment:
THE PRINCIPLE Verification is a SECOND AXIS, orthogonal to status. An item can be CLEAR and UNVERIFIED at the same moment, and pretending otherwise is the failure mode this page exists to avoid. So the two axes get two entirely separate visual channels: - STATUS is chromatic — volt, gold, ember, magenta, dim. - VERIFICATION is achromatic — a hatched or solid ink rule, an outlined mono tag, and a dotted underline. Spending no accent on verification buys three things for free: the two layers can never collide or be confused; the treatment survives every colour vision deficiency by construction; and it prints in black on a mono laser printer with zero loss, which is what the lawyer will actually be holding. THE FIVE RULES, ENFORCED IN THE BUILD 1. Never hidden. UNVERIFIED is never behind a `
`, a tooltip, a hover, an asterisk, a footnote number, or a "see appendix". It sits inline, in the row, above the fold of that row, at every viewport width. 2. Never colour-only, never hover-only. Three simultaneous carriers: the 4px hatched left rule on the containing row/cell/tile, the outlined `UNVERIFIED` mono tag, and the claim restated in plain words. 3. Always has a way out. Every unverified fact carries a `settles` string — the specific document, rule cite, or person that would resolve it. The build FAILS if an unverified fact has no `settles` value. "Unverified" without "what would settle it" is a shrug, not a disclosure; this mirrors the "What would settle it" convention already used throughout `public/product/investor/numbers.md`. 4. Always counted, never netted out. The masthead, every region header, and every progress meter carry a live unverified count. No percentage is ever printed on this page without its unverified count in the same breath. 5. Always escalated into a question. Every unverified fact is automatically collected into §09 Open questions for counsel, numbered Q1…Qn, sorted by the money and days that hang on the answer. An unknown that generates no question is a build error. THE ARITHMETIC RULE — the honesty guardrail An item that is TICKED but whose legal basis is UNVERIFIED does not count toward the verified-done segment of any progress meter. It fills its own hatched segment. The label reads "14/38 done · 6 on an unverified basis · 9 blocked". This makes it structurally impossible for the page to show a comfortable bar that is resting on guesses — which is the single most likely way a compliance checklist lies to its own author. THE THREE FORMS BLOCK (a whole item, jurisdiction, or matrix cell) — the row takes `data-verify="unverified"`, which paints a 4px left rule of `repeating-linear-gradient(45deg, color-mix(in oklab, var(--text) 42%, transparent) 0 2px, transparent 2px 5px)`, and the row contains: UNVERIFIED · "That a federal MSB registration is required for M2." · "Settles it: FinCEN 31 CFR 1010.100(ff) read against the prize-pool flow, or written counsel." · [Question 7] The tag is `var(--font-mono)`, `var(--fs-12)`, letter-spacing .12em, `var(--text)` on `var(--bg-2)` with a 1px `color-mix(in oklab, var(--text) 55%, transparent)` border and `var(--r-control)`. The claim line is `--fs-14` `--text`; the settles line is `--fs-14` `--muted` with a mono `--fs-12` `--dim` "SETTLES IT:" label. The settles line is never collapsed at any width — it is the sentence that makes the disclosure useful. INLINE (one value inside otherwise-verified prose) — `approx.`: `text-decoration: underline dotted 1px`, `text-underline-offset: 3px`, decoration colour `color-mix(in oklab, var(--text) 55%, transparent)`, plus `::after { content: " ?"; font-family: var(--font-mono); color: var(--dim) }` so it is not a hover-only or decoration-only signal. On touch, activating it writes its `data-settle` text into the live region — `title` is never the sole carrier, because `title` does not exist on a phone. TILE (a jurisdiction whose status is a guess) — the tile keeps its status tint and takes the same achromatic hatched left rule. Its screen-reader text ends "— unverified". A state whose status is a guess must never look like a state whose status is researched. UNKNOWN vs UNVERIFIED — a distinction the page keeps - UNKNOWN is a status: nobody has looked. It renders as the dim dashed chip or the `—` / `UNKNOWN` pair inside a `dd`, never a blank cell, never `$0`, never "TBD". - UNVERIFIED is a verification flag: we have an answer but we cannot stand behind its source. Both count toward the page's unverified tally and both generate a question. They are separate words because the remedy differs — one needs research, the other needs a source or counsel. WHERE THE COUNT SURFACES Masthead ("UNVERIFIED 23"), every region header ("Unverified 9 facts"), the "Unverified only" filter chip in the sticky bar, every progress label, the print cover block, and §09's heading ("23 open questions"). Six places, one number, computed from one source — the JSON — so it can never drift. PRINT Hatching is unreliable at print DPI, so in print the rule becomes a solid 2px black left border with `print-color-adjust: exact` applied to that rule alone; the tag prints as `[UNVERIFIED]` in black mono inside a 1px black box; the dotted inline underline survives as-is and its `data-settle` prints as a parenthetical after the value (`.fd-u::after { content: " (unverified: " attr(data-settle) ")" }`). Nothing about the verification layer depends on colour reaching the paper.
